1e5bc58a-d7dd-4dbf-8f89-9ae903f3aa8e.name: Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management
1e5bc58a-d7dd-4dbf-8f89-9ae903f3aa8e.description: This Advanced Diploma is designed for students who have completed the Diploma of Hospitality Management and want to move into hospitality management or business-owner roles. It builds skills to plan, lead and deliver hospitality operations across a range of venue types, with expanded coverage of business planning, finance, human resources, marketing and physical asset management. Teaching is delivered by experienced hospitality professionals and industry guest lecturers who bring real-world insight into the classroom, and the qualification is designed as a direct progression from Angliss's own Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT50422).
1e5bc58a-d7dd-4dbf-8f89-9ae903f3aa8e.curriculum: Core units (SIT60322): SITXHRM010 Recruit, select and induct staff; BSBOPS601 Develop and implement business plans; SITXMPR014 Develop and implement marketing strategies; BSBFIN601 Manage organisational finances; SITXHRM012 Monitor staff performance; SITXFIN011 Manage physical assets; SITXWHS008 Establish and maintain a work health and safety system.
1e5bc58a-d7dd-4dbf-8f89-9ae903f3aa8e.admission_requirements: William Angliss Institute's international entry requirements for Certificate, Diploma and Advanced Diploma level courses require an Australian Year 12 qualification with satisfactory results and attendance, or an equivalent senior secondary certificate with satisfactory results, or a recognised Foundation Studies program completed in Australia, or the International Baccalaureate Diploma (minimum 23 points), or Cambridge Overseas School Certificate/GCE O Level passes in at least 5 subjects with a minimum of 4 Cs.
1e5bc58a-d7dd-4dbf-8f89-9ae903f3aa8e.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (no band less than 5.0), or equivalent: PTE Academic 47, CAE (C1 Advanced) 161, or TOEFL iBT overall 67.

c6506fde-84d8-4917-8e03-02e179f9c664.name: Associate Degree in Culinary Management
c6506fde-84d8-4917-8e03-02e179f9c664.description: This hands-on culinary program gives students the skills and experience to start a career in food and hospitality, covering everything from gourmet cuisine to fine wine while learning to work in culinary teams. Students learn directly from leading chefs, artisan producers and industry experts, with practical challenges, real-world case studies and guest speakers sharing current industry trends. Electives allow students to tailor their studies, and the course is designed to feed directly into Angliss's own Bachelor of Culinary Management for students who want to continue their studies.
c6506fde-84d8-4917-8e03-02e179f9c664.curriculum: Year 1: CUL501 Cookery and Recipes; CUL504 Understanding Food Service; MAN501 Management Fundamentals; MAN504 Financial Knowledge and Decision Making; CUL502 Culinary Techniques; GAS659 Cooks and Chefs in Society; MAN505 Marketing and Consumer Behaviour; 1 elective. Year 2: CUL604 Advanced Culinary Techniques; HOS605 Menu Design and Engineering; MAN606 Human Resource Operations for the Services Industry; CUL602 Restaurant Service; HOS606 Australian Wine in Hospitality; MAN711 Data Analysis and Communication; 2 electives. All students must complete a self-paced online Foundation Academic Communication Skills module (UGRASP) within the first six weeks of their first semester, unless otherwise agreed.
c6506fde-84d8-4917-8e03-02e179f9c664.admission_requirements: William Angliss Institute's own course page for the Associate Degree in Culinary Management links to the same Higher Education Admissions Transparency policy used for its Bachelor's degrees, rather than to its VET-level entry table. Under that policy, eligibility for entry is demonstrated by ATAR score, previous higher education or VET study, work experience or other factors; individual course admission criteria also apply. William Angliss's separate international entry-requirements page sets the equivalent international academic bar for Bachelor-level (and, per this course page's own linking, Associate Degree) courses as an Australian Year 12 qualification with an ATAR/TER of 50 or higher, a recognised Foundation Studies program completed with a credit average, the International Baccalaureate Diploma (minimum 25 points over six subjects), or a Cambridge GCE Advanced Level Certificate with grade D or higher in 3 Advanced Level subjects.
c6506fde-84d8-4917-8e03-02e179f9c664.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent: PTE Academic 47, CAE (C1 Advanced) 161, or TOEFL iBT overall 67. This is the Bachelor tier of William Angliss's published international English-language table; the Institute's own course page groups this Associate Degree with its Bachelor's degrees under the same Higher Education Admissions Transparency policy rather than its separate VET (Certificate/Diploma/Advanced Diploma) entry table.

58411896-0f66-4775-a4b9-3b5149618151.name: Associate Degree in Tourism
58411896-0f66-4775-a4b9-3b5149618151.description: The Associate Degree in Tourism gives students a solid understanding of the structure and operating environment of the tourism industry, developing analytical skills, critical thinking, problem solving and communication alongside the fundamental principles and theories of tourism. Students study operations and risk management, economic and global impacts and marketing, underpinned by field trips to Victorian tourist destinations and attractions and direct learning from industry leaders. Graduates are equipped to pursue further academic study, including progression into Angliss's own tourism degrees, or move directly into the tourism industry.

eef3714e-f3ec-4a24-bc5e-6e410e0be4c2.description: This associate degree covers the fast-paced world of tourism and hospitality, building the skills to supervise people, operations and experiences across restaurants, hotels, resorts, attractions and destinations. Learning combines practice in live classrooms and industry-standard facilities with real-world insight from industry specialists and guest speakers, plus field trips to venues, wineries and attractions. 975e78f7-8dc5-49de-bda1-8bd00159a0a7.description: This three-year degree blends real-world culinary experience with academic study, building the practical skills needed to succeed in professional culinary teams and confidence in fast-paced kitchen environments. Students strengthen kitchen techniques, expand their understanding of food culture, and develop the leadership and business skills required to lead teams, manage processes and launch a career in the food industry, with a range of electives available to shape an individual career path. Graduates step into the industry with the skills, knowledge and leadership capability to manage people, drive innovation and make their mark as culinary professionals. Students wanting an additional practical placement year can instead take Angliss's separate Bachelor of Culinary Management (Professional Practice), a distinct four-year course.

352e886b-b26f-4174-9902-878b1ee7be5d.name: Bachelor of Event Management (Diploma to Degree Pathway)
352e886b-b26f-4174-9902-878b1ee7be5d.description: This is a packaged pathway course, not a standalone direct-entry bachelor's degree: students complete the Diploma of Event Management (SIT50322) in Year 1, then articulate directly into Year 2 and Year 3 of the Bachelor of Event Management, graduating with both qualifications after three years total. The diploma year covers hands-on event operations, coordinating real events and industry placement opportunities, while the degree years build strategic and management-level skills, including business events, digital event design and major events and logistics, supported by field trips to festivals, business events and hotel conference venues. Angliss's strong industry connections give students the chance to work on real projects and take on meaningful roles with leading organisations while building their professional network.
352e886b-b26f-4174-9902-878b1ee7be5d.curriculum: Year 1: SIT50322 Diploma of Event Management (full VET diploma, completed as the packaged first year). Year 2: Academic Preparation course (online); Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (Business Events); Designing Memorable Experiences; Human Resource Operations for the Services Industry; Social and Lifestyle Events; Data Analysis and Communication; 3 electives. Year 3: Digital Event Design; Sustainability in the Tourism and Hospitality Industry; Innovation and Entrepreneurship; Major Events and Logistics; Critical Challenges Hub; 5 electives.
352e886b-b26f-4174-9902-878b1ee7be5d.admission_requirements: Eligibility for entry can be demonstrated by ATAR score, previous study, work experience and other factors, per William Angliss Institute's Higher Education Admissions Transparency policy. 352e886b-b26f-4174-9902-878b1ee7be5d.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent: PTE Academic 47, CAE (C1 Advanced) 161, or TOEFL iBT overall 67. 851b8368-90eb-470b-a8c4-72b28d03702c.name: Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management
851b8368-90eb-470b-a8c4-72b28d03702c.description: This three-year degree prepares students for leadership roles in the international resort and hotel industry, combining specialist hospitality subjects with core management skills in people management, financial decision making, resort operations and data analytics. Students learn how the industry works and how to adapt as business models, technology and guest expectations evolve, supported by industry professionals in the classroom and field trips and site visits to hotels and resorts across Melbourne and regional Victoria. Simulations and industry-standard technology build the skills to analyse, innovate and lead. Two further, separately coded Angliss degrees extend this course with an additional placement or international-study year: the Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management (Professional Practice) and the Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management (International Practice).

d60823bb-6795-4311-807d-36039a821ef5.description: This three-year degree builds the skills, knowledge and real-world experience to manage people, operations and experiences across hospitality and tourism, from local attractions to global destinations. This diploma is delivered by food industry specialists across multiple disciplines who bring real-world experience into the classroom, and includes field trips, experiential learning, a major product development project and networking opportunities to build insight into the science behind food manufacturing and successful food businesses.

2beffccd-2452-4a66-a825-4b54b769c85e.name: Diploma of Hospitality Management
2beffccd-2452-4a66-a825-4b54b769c85e.description: Designed for students building a future in restaurant and venue operations, this diploma covers business operations, finance, human resources and service quality alongside the practical skills needed to create memorable service experiences. Students are taught by experienced hospitality professionals and hear from a diverse range of guest lecturers who share current industry insights, with opportunities to get involved in Melbourne events such as the Melbourne Food and Wine Festival and the Australian Grand Prix. 206bdb1b-ed55-491c-b668-2bc3da0d486e.name: Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management
206bdb1b-ed55-491c-b668-2bc3da0d486e.description: This diploma prepares students for management roles in travel and tourism, covering business operations, regulations, sustainable practices and planning alongside practical, hands-on experience. Students explore metropolitan and regional destinations, visit tourism operators, hear from experienced professionals and guest speakers, and get the chance to lead their own tour. An optional industry placement (requiring application and interview) is available for students who want further real-world experience before graduating with the skills, knowledge and connections to start a career in travel and tourism.

fc599628-a3cf-4834-8118-6c4c4d82cd0b.name: Graduate Certificate of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship
fc599628-a3cf-4834-8118-6c4c4d82cd0b.description: This graduate certificate builds the mindset and skills to turn entrepreneurial ambition into reality in a global hospitality setting, developing innovative thinking, confident leadership and sound decision making. Studying at an institute focused on hospitality, students innovate, iterate and solve real-world industry challenges through hands-on learning, developing a growth mindset, self-belief and the drive to lead people and ideas forward. Graduates are prepared to apply entrepreneurial thinking, reflect on their decisions and create opportunities in the international hospitality industry.
fc599628-a3cf-4834-8118-6c4c4d82cd0b.curriculum: Year 1: LED851 Leading Self and Others; LED852 People and Culture Driven Leadership; MAN801 Financial Management and Data Analytics; ENT809 Entrepreneurial Mindset, Practices and Experiences.
fc599628-a3cf-4834-8118-6c4c4d82cd0b.admission_requirements: Available on application. William Angliss Institute's own course page states entry requirements for this Graduate Certificate are assessed individually on application rather than against a single published academic bar.

4bbe84a7-f4e1-4b63-9914-da62290cd6d1.name: Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership
4bbe84a7-f4e1-4b63-9914-da62290cd6d1.description: Designed for aspiring leaders in the global hotel and resort industry, this graduate diploma helps students build the confidence and capability to lead with impact, developing essential leadership skills alongside practical knowledge in hotel operations, finance, people management and business strategy. 85c4f4f8-a1ec-4846-aa0d-10fdf1661e10.name: Master of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship
85c4f4f8-a1ec-4846-aa0d-10fdf1661e10.description: This master's degree features industry experts giving students the opportunity to learn, observe, question and receive feedback from accomplished hospitality start-up founders, representatives and venture capitalists. It aims to develop and elevate an entrepreneurial mindset to drive innovation and sustainability in the hospitality industry, with students evaluating financing options, learning to build high-performance teams and fostering a dynamic culture that embraces innovation. The course cultivates entrepreneurial leadership capacity through experiential learning, and the final year provides the opportunity to demonstrate a strategic entrepreneurial focus via a work placement.
85c4f4f8-a1ec-4846-aa0d-10fdf1661e10.curriculum: Year 1 (shared with the Graduate Diploma of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship): LED851 Leading Self and Others; LED852 People and Culture Driven Leadership; MAN801 Financial Management and Data Analytics; ENT809 Entrepreneurial Mindset, Practices and Experiences; ENT819 Financing Entrepreneurial Ventures; MAN901 Design Thinking for the Experience Economy; ENT829 Entrepreneurial Leadership and Innovation; 1 elective in semester 2. Year 2: LED951 Leadership in Uncertain Times; ENT909 Strategic Entrepreneurship; ENT917 Entrepreneurial Incubator: From Idea to Pre-launch; 1 elective in semester 2; PRP918 Professional Practice (work placement).
85c4f4f8-a1ec-4846-aa0d-10fdf1661e10.admission_requirements: Successful completion of a Bachelor Degree equivalent to AQF Level 7 in a related field (Hospitality, Tourism, Culinary or Hotel Management); or successful completion of a Bachelor Degree in an unrelated field plus relevant supervisory or management work experience in the hospitality, tourism, culinary or hotel industry, demonstrated via a current CV, professional awards or memberships (an interview may be required), per William Angliss Institute's published international entry requirements.
85c4f4f8-a1ec-4846-aa0d-10fdf1661e10.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent: PTE Academic 58, CAE (C1 Advanced) 176 (no less than 169 in any component), or TOEFL iBT overall 79.

8274dfa3-51be-4246-acdd-41f9cc1b1830.name: Master of International Hotel Leadership
8274dfa3-51be-4246-acdd-41f9cc1b1830.description: This interdisciplinary master's degree helps students grow into confident, future-ready hotel leaders, learning through real-world, practical experiences while working with industry experts to tackle real business challenges set by industry leaders. Students build practical business strategy skills, lead creativity and innovation in international hotel environments, and learn to foster positive workplace cultures that drive high performance. In the final year, students bring it all together by applying leadership theory via a work placement. Graduates are recognised as agile leaders ready to drive change, innovate and implement sustainable, high-impact solutions in the global hotel industry.
8274dfa3-51be-4246-acdd-41f9cc1b1830.curriculum: Year 1 (shared with the Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership): LED851 Leading Self and Others; LED852 People and Culture Driven Leadership; MAN801 Financial Management and Data Analytics; HOH809 International Hotel Operations Management; HOH859 Global and Ethical Hotel Leadership; MAN809 Revenue Management and Strategy; RES801 Research Methods elective subject; 1 elective in semester 2. Year 2: HOH918 Work Placement (prerequisite RES801); LED951 Leadership in Uncertain Times; HOH909 Leading Sustainability in the Hotel Industry; MAN901 Design Thinking for the Experience Economy; 1 elective in semester 2.

8274dfa3-51be-4246-acdd-41f9cc1b1830.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent: PTE Academic 58, CAE (C1 Advanced) 176 (no less than 169 in any component), or TOEFL iBT overall 79.
